history.summary: CRITICAL CSV FLAG: there is no verified ISKCON temple in Kohima. The only ISKCON temple documented in Nagaland is at Signal Bosti, Dimapur (Dimapur district), consecrated/established in 1995 CE per inheritage.foundation - so the CSV town 'Kohima' appears to be wrong and this file documents the Dimapur temple as the best-supported referent; the dataset owner should correct the town or merge this row. The temple is dedicated to Lord Krishna, built in a modern interpretation of the Orissan Nagara / broader Nagara style with a curvilinear shikhara, and is maintained by the ISKCON Foundation with daily rituals, festivals and community programmes. Coordinates are the Signal Bosti locality pin, not the exact shrine pin (verify). Media is empty: no image verifiably depicting the Dimapur ISKCON temple was found after genuine searching.

town_description: Dimapur is the largest city and commercial hub of Nagaland, on the plains bordering Assam. It holds the Kachari Ruins (Dimasa kingdom), the Dimapur Kalibari, the ISKCON temple at Signal Bosti, and the Swayambhu Shiva temple at Singrijan; Dimapur Airport and the railway station connect it to Guwahati, Kolkata and Delhi.
